title: 4.2 kiloyear event
summary: About 4,200 years ago climate records show an abrupt shift to cooler, drier conditions, known as the 4.2 ka event; one article notes it coincides with the migration and collapse of many early civilizations. A stalagmite from Mawmluh Cave in Meghalaya, India, is the international reference for the start of the Meghalayan Age, ratified in 2018.

uncertainty.note: The Meghalayan lower boundary is 4250 years before 2000 CE (Head 2019, cited by PAGES), giving astronomical year -2250. The Conversation says 4,200 years ago. The opened pages give no end date or error bar.

where.historical_name: Mawmluh Cave near Cherrapunji in Meghalaya, northeast India; no unified polity at this date

importance.justification: A widely cited abrupt climate shift, used to define the start of the Meghalayan Age.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: the id says 2200 BCE, but the boundary is given as 4250 years before 2000 CE (astronomical year -2250) and The Conversation says 4,200 years ago. The pin is the Mawmluh Cave stalagmite, the sourced type section, with 5 km uncertainty for the cave; the event itself is wider. The civilization-collapse link is only noted as coincidence on the opened page, not established.
